title: Methanol meets oxygen
hook: Count the atoms before the molecules change partners.

knows: Atoms of an element are conserved in ordinary chemical reactions.
doesNotKnow: How molecule counts and atom counts differ in this balanced reaction.

misconception: The number of molecules must stay constant when atoms rearrange.
objective: Use atom counts to explain 2 CH₃OH + 3 O₂ → 2 CO₂ + 4 H₂O.

claims.text: Question, stage and reveal: Complete combustion of methanol produces carbon dioxide and water. 2 CH₃OH + 3 O₂ → 2 CO₂ + 4 H₂O; The model gives 4 H₂O: 2 CH₃OH + 3 O₂ → 2 CO₂ + 4 H₂O. The 2 C, 8 H, 8 O atoms are present on both sides; atoms change partners, not identity.
claims.source: OpenStax Chemistry 2e §4.1 https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/4-1-writing-and-balancing-chemical-equations; reaction model balanced by counting each element. Specific reaction identity needs independent verification.

claims.text: Each circle is one atom, grouped by molecular formula; the diagram is not a molecular geometry or real-time reaction mechanism.
Recall: doubling every coefficient gives 8 H₂O molecules.
claims.source: Multiply every coefficient in 2 CH₃OH + 3 O₂ → 2 CO₂ + 4 H₂O by two.

recall.question: If you double every starting amount in 2 CH₃OH + 3 O₂ → 2 CO₂ + 4 H₂O, how many H₂O molecules are produced in the same model?
recall.why: Doubling the starting amounts doubles each product coefficient in this model.
